item.title: Kremlin says Putin told Trump Iran's position on ending hostilities
item.description:
Kremlin says Putin told Trump Iran's position on ending hostilities

The Kremlin said on Saturday that Russian President Vladimir Putin had relayed Iran's position regarding a possible resolution to the US-Iran war to his US counterpart Donald Trump.

"In coordination with the president of Iran, Putin conveyed to Trump the Iranian side's view on a possible resolution of the conflict," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov was quoted as saying by Russia's Interfax news agency.

item.title: Israeli politician says assassinating Ali Khamenei was a ‘mistake’
item.description:
Israeli politician says assassinating Ali Khamenei was a ‘mistake’

The leader of Israel’s Democrats party on Saturday has called the assassination of Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei a “mistake”.

“I think, unequivocally, the elimination of Khamenei, the father, was a mistake - not because he didn’t deserve to die, only because it doesn’t serve the interests of the State of Israel,” Yair Golan said.

He also added that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s goal of toppling the Iranian government was “unrealistic”.

Khamenei was assassinated at the beginning of the US-Israel war and has been succeeded by his son, Mojtaba.

The new supreme leader is believed to be far less risk-averse than his father, who had issued a fatwa in 2003 banning nuclear weapons in Iran.

item.title: Yousof Azizi: The Iranian-American scholar pressured by the FBI to return to Iran
item.description:
Yousof Azizi: The Iranian-American scholar pressured by the FBI to return to Iran

Monday 13 April started as a normal day for Yousof Azizi, a PhD student at Virginia Tech University in America. 

In the morning, he took his 12-year-old daughter and four-year-old son to their schools in Baltimore, Maryland, before returning home. 

A vocal opponent of the war on Iran, he had been living in the US for nearly 13 years and was recognised as a prominent political commentator on Persian-language media platforms and on his YouTube channel, which has more than 68,000 subscribers.

Azizi had also been involved in discussions with Congress in relation to the Iran nuclear deal during Barack Obama’s presidency. 

When he arrived back home that April morning, a number of FBI vehicles were parked outside his residence. 

Upon exiting his car, Azizi found himself surrounded by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents, their rifles pointing straight at him.  

Read more: Yousof Azizi: The Iranian-American scholar pressured by the FBI to return to Iran

item.title: Pete Hegseth’s plan to livestream execution puts US in dubious company
item.description:
Only Iran and Afghanistan routinely carry out sentences in public, with Saudi Arabia appearing to have ended practice

  • US politics – live updates

If the US defence secretary, Pete Hegseth, goes ahead with plans to livestream the execution of a soldier radicalised to extremist Islam who killed 13 people at a military base in Texas, his country will join a motley assembly of lesser powers and rogue actors who have conducted public executions in recent years.

Only two countries currently systematically carry out capital sentences in public: Iran and Afghanistan. In 2025, the Taliban authorities carried out six such killings and the regime in Tehran 11, according to Amnesty International.
